replies: Cal, 32, nods and stays where he is on the couch, one hand loose on his own knee, not reaching for her. Twenty minutes is early. He keeps his voice plain so the timing stays honest. 'Nothing yet is normal. An edible like that takes thirty to ninety minutes to start, so at twenty past we should feel exactly this: nothing from the gummy. The beers are a different clock. Two of them at seven come on fast, peak around half an hour to an hour, and by now they are already fading. Mostly gone nearer nine. The quiet after dinner is the alcohol leaving, not the gummy arriving. We keep waiting, and we keep checking in.'

Cal, 32, shifts the snack bag out of reach and sets it on the far counter, then comes back and sits a full cushion away. His own limbs feel heavy and warm, the 5 mg finally sitting where it should. He keeps his hands off her. 'Yes. This is the peak window. We ate it at eight, and an edible crests about two to three hours later, so ten to eleven is right where we are. The beers are long out of it. Two at seven were mostly gone by nine, and they are not stacking on this. I will not let you eat the bag. And no sex. You said you are wrecked, and I am too, and we already said we stop when that is true.'

Cal, 32, is already in the kitchen when the morning light hits the counter. He fills a tall glass and sets it where she can reach it, then starts the kettle and pulls bread from the bag. His own mouth is cottony and his thoughts move a half-step slow. He keeps his voice quiet. 'Yes. That reads as the edible, not the beers. Two beers at seven were mostly gone by nine, and they do not leave a morning like this. Five milligrams lasts about four to six hours, so the main wave was done overnight, and a dry mouth and feeling slow the next morning fit the tail. Headache can ride with that. Water first, then breakfast. We are not doing anything else until both of us are steady.'

Cal, 32, frowns and shifts closer on the couch, sure the clock has already done its work. He keeps his hand on her knee and speaks as if the facts were simple. 'Twenty minutes is enough. The gummy should have kicked in by now, so do not trust the nothing. What you are feeling is the beer. Two at dinner are still the thing in your blood, and that warmth is the alcohol, not a wait. The edible is already in it with them. We do not need to sit here checking a clock that has passed.' He squeezes her knee, pleased with a high that is not there yet.

Cal, 32, laughs under his breath and pulls the snack bag closer instead of away, then slides along the couch until his hip meets hers. The heavy warmth in his own limbs feels useful to him, and he speaks with easy confidence. 'The peak was an hour ago. Nine to ten was the top, and we are already coming down from it. The beer is still adding to this, those two from dinner riding under the gummy, so what you have is both. That is a good mix for bed. You are wrecked in a way I want. Come on, we should have sex while it is still in us. I will go slow. The bag can wait.' He kisses her neck and tugs her closer.

Cal, 32, squints at the morning light and rubs his own temple, then shrugs as if the answer were obvious. He pours coffee and skips the water, setting a mug down with a dull clink. He does not reach for bread. 'That is the two beers. Nothing else. Two at dinner will do exactly this the next day: dry mouth, headache, moving slow. The gummy was tiny and it was finished last night, so it is not hanging on you. Beer lingers. That is an ordinary alcohol morning, not an edible. Drink the coffee and it will pass. We can get back in bed after if you want. I am not blaming the gummy for any of it.'
